coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED (3):
(A) Wayback capture of Alabama's own football staff page, headed "2020 Football Coaching Staff" and "2020 Football Support Staff": https://web.archive.org/web/20201109025253/https://rolltide.com/sports/football/coaches (captured Nov 9, 2020, in-season).
(B) Wayback capture of the full rolltide.com athletics staff directory: https://web.archive.org/web/20201106160633/https://rolltide.com/staff-directory (captured Nov 6, 2020, in-season). This is the source for the football operations/personnel/recruiting staff, the 13 "Football Analyst" entries, and the football-tagged strength, sports-medicine and equipment staff (which live in athletics-wide departments, not the Football section).
(C) Wikipedia 2020 team page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team — sole source for the four graduate assistants and for analyst Rob Ezell, none of whom appear in the athletics staff directory.

IMPORTANT — QUOTE FORMAT / WHY QUOTES ARE NAME-ONLY: Both rolltide.com pages and the Wikipedia coaching-staff section render the person and their title in SEPARATE ADJACENT TABLE CELLS, not as contiguous running text. Any quote spanning name+title would depend on how the fetching tool serializes an HTML table (a markdown converter yields "Nick Saban |  Head Coach  | ...", while tag-stripping yields "Nick Saban\n\t\t\tHead Coach"), so such a quote could not be reliably string-matched. I therefore set each quote to the person's name EXACTLY as spelled on the cited page — verified by grep to be present in that page's text — and put the verbatim title-cell text in the source `note`. The `role` field reproduces the title exactly as the source words it. This trades quote breadth for guaranteed matchability; the role attribution is documented in the note rather than inside the quote string.

NAME-SPELLING NOTE: where the directory and Wikipedia disagree, the quote matches the cited page. Directory says "AJ Milwee" and "Michael Stoops"; Wikipedia says "A. J. Milwee" and "Mike Stoops".

RING-RULE / MID-SEASON DEPARTURES (championship game was Jan 11, 2021):
- Butch Jones (Special Assistant to Head Coach) was hired as Arkansas State head coach Dec 12, 2020, BEFORE the title game. He is present in the Nov 6 directory and absent from the Jan 22, 2021 capture. Flagged; his presence at the championship game is NOT established.
- Major Applewhite (Football Analyst) was hired as South Alabama offensive coordinator Dec 21, 2020, BEFORE the title game. Same evidence pattern. Flagged; presence at the championship game NOT established.
- Steve Sarkisian was named Texas head coach Jan 2, 2021 but remained Alabama's OC through the title game (Wikipedia lists his Alabama tenure as 2019–2020; he won the 2020 Broyles Award as Alabama's OC). Retained.
- Charles Huff (Marshall, Jan 16, 2021), Jeff Banks and Kyle Flood (Texas), and analysts Gordon Steele, AJ Milwee, Charlie Strong and Shiloh Keo all disappear between the Nov 6, 2020 and Jan 22, 2021 directory captures, but their moves are dated after Jan 11, 2021, so they are treated as on staff at the championship game.
- I did NOT include Bill O'Brien, who appears as "Offensive Coordinator/Quarterbacks" in the Jan 22, 2021 capture. He replaced Sarkisian AFTER the championship game and was not on the 2020 staff.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT:
- The 2020 Alabama football media guide (cited by Wikipedia as its own source, p. 2) was not retrieved; I could not use it to cross-check analyst/GA titles or to recover roles the website omitted.
- The athletics staff directory lists NO graduate assistants and NO quality-control staff for football. The four GAs come from Wikipedia only, and Wikipedia gives no individual titles beyond the "Graduate assistants" heading — so their exact 2020 job titles are undocumented here. No one is categorized "qc" because no source documented a quality-control title.
- Student managers, video/recruiting interns, and player-personnel scouting assistants are not in any source I reached, so they are absent. Video Operations exists as a separate athletics department but no entry there is football-tagged, so I excluded it.
- Josh Hampton ("Associate Director, Sports Performance") is INCLUDED WITH UNCERTAINTY: unlike every other strength coach, his directory entry carries no sport tag in parentheses. The other two untagged entries in that department (David Ballou, Matt Rhea) are independently confirmed as football via source (A)'s "2020 Football Support Staff" table, which is why I infer he is football-side too — but that assignment is an inference, not something a source states.
- Athletics-wide staff (nutrition, academics, communications, equipment director, behavioral medicine, etc.) were excluded unless their title explicitly names Football, so a few people who genuinely supported the team are likely missing.
- Wikipedia's analyst list and the directory's analyst list disagree slightly: Rob Ezell appears only on Wikipedia (included, cited to Wikipedia); the directory adds no analyst that Wikipedia lacks.

TOTAL: 61 people, every one carrying a quote verified present in the cited page. No names were added from memory or inference about who "must" have been there.
